selection_reason: Token graph contracts and build outputs are testable in this environment; responsive/browser-dependent work follows in round 03. Priority remains P1.
question: How do typed token aliases, semantic roles, theme overrides, and CSS emission fail while appearing superficially consistent?
research_questions: Where are current authoritative interchange and variable-resolution contracts maintained?
Which type, reference, cycle and fallback cases must a consumer reject or explicitly leave unsupported?
Which semantic role and theme decisions are engineering policy versus requirements of the format?
How can we compare baseline and candidate using malformed, boundary and valid token graphs?
rubric: Resolve a supported acyclic typed alias graph deterministically
Reject missing targets, cycles, incompatible types and unsupported constructs clearly
Preserve semantic token roles across all declared themes without choosing a new art direction
Reject generated CSS name collisions or ambiguous exports
Never treat successful config resolution as rendered contrast, forced-colors or WCAG conformance
decision: ACCEPT only narrowly defined tested graph/contract behavior; browser visual effects HOLD; failed probes REVISE
